purpose: Promote proven lifecycle fragments into AUZiX package metadata and rebuild or repackage the affected packages.

tracks.when: Temporary bridge/rescue only, or the source-build receipt already proves this exact payload was produced by the correct configure/build/install contract.
steps: load existing package artifact
mark migration stage as bridge/staging unless a matching source-build receipt exists
preserve payload tgz unless validation proves payload defect
merge lifecycle.json from promoted fragments
apply AUZiX path/export matrix
add or update command wrappers and desktop entries
add validation probes and receipt expectations
refresh package index
run install plus setup validation in AUZiX validation host

tracks.when: The binary payload has incorrect paths, missing linked libraries, wrong compile-time assumptions, or non-portable hardwired paths.
steps: inspect Debian source contract
extract configure/build/install arguments
run the native Debian build once as a guidebook when needed
apply AUZiX path policy before build output is packaged
run configure/cmake/meson with AUZiX prefix, sysconfdir, localstatedir, libdir, bindir, and pkg-config values
run make/ninja build
run make/ninja install into a staging root with DESTDIR or the build-system equivalent
record configure/build/install command lines, environment, logs, staged file manifest, and checksums
build dependencies in dependency order
run strings, ldd, stat, command smoke, and lifecycle setup probes
publish only if validation passes

initial_candidates.reason: Desktop stack needs authoritative system/session bus lifecycle setup and status probes.
Flatpak, LightDM, and privileged desktop tools need policies and daemon readiness.
Greeter, PAM, X11 session, input-device groups, and session handoff need repeatable setup.
Efreet, icons, MIME, desktop database, and cache refresh hooks explain many menu/launcher regressions.
Session wrapper, XDG path export, theme/menu cache, and validation probes need to live with the package.
System helper, portals, remotes, dbus, polkit, and /var compatibility assumptions must be explicit.
CLI tools work partially, but Impress/Draw/library and launcher failures suggest payload and wrapper validation still need a clean source-contract pass.
Runtime crashes, CA/font drift, and sandbox warnings need source and runtime lifecycle evidence before another blind package pass.
